To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the size and N application rate of sheep urine patches significantly influenced the cumulative N2O emission from urine patches, but that the N2O emission factor was similar when a high N concentration urine patch was applied at 200 kg/ha N and a low N concentration urine patch applied at 800 kg/ha N.
the size and N application rate of sheep urine patches influence N2O emissions and that the IPCC default of N2O emissions of 1% of N excreted by grazing sheep may be too high.

(i) N2O emissions were greater when urine was applied in four small patches compared with one larger patch at 800 kg/ha N loading rate; (ii) the amount of N applied, rather than urine N concentration, was the main driver of N2O emissions; (iii) N2O emission factor was lower (10 times) than the IPCC default value for sheep excretes; and (iv) further research is required on the typical volumes of urine deposited by sheep

the size of the urine patch and the amount of N applied per patch can influence N2O emissions; therefore, these factors should be considered in models predicting N2O emissions and in management decisions aimed at mitigating N2O emissions.
